parts.text:
{
  "first_impression": "It's an unexpectedly tense and charming herding sim that nails the core fantasy of being a working border collie. The clean low-poly look and Scottish pastoral vibe immediately grab you, though the bird's-eye camera can feel a bit sterile compared to the pretty ground-level vistas. Once the wolves show up and the weather kicks in, it shifts from relaxing stroll to frantic plate-spinning faster than I anticipated.",
  "scores": {
    "visual_appeal": 7,
    "readability": 8,
    "game_feel": 7,
    "fun_factor": 8,
    "variety": 8,
    "sense_of_progression": 7,
    "want_to_keep_playing": 8,
    "would_wishlist": 8
  },
  "best_things": [
    "The escalation of mechanics across the season - from stubborn rams and lost lambs to flooded bridges and blizzard visibility - keeps each run fresh.",
    "The wolf snatch alerts and rescue dashes create genuine adrenaline without breaking the cozy countryside aesthetic.",
    "The charm system and the ability to command a second veteran dog (Old Fly) add real tactical depth to what could have been a shallow gimmick."
  ],
  "worst_problems": [
    {
      "problem": "The camera defaults to an almost clinical top-down satellite view, stripping away the gorgeous atmospheric landscapes teased during cutscenes.",
      "where": "00:10 to 00:26 vs 00:27",
      "severity": "major",
      "suggestion": "Give us a dynamic isometric tilt or an adjustable third-person camera toggle during normal gameplay so we can actually see the horizon and sunset while playing."
    },
    {
      "problem": "Sheep pathfinding through narrow gates and bridges gets clunky, leading to awkward bottleneck bunching where sheep grind against fences.",
      "where": "02:45, 08:23, 12:26",
      "severity": "major",
      "suggestion": "Smooth out the flock fluid dynamics around chokepoints and gate posts so sheep naturally funnel instead of clipping and sticking to collision edges."
    },
    {
      "problem": "UI alerts and UI popups (like wolf distance meters and tutorial prompts) stack heavily in the center of the screen, creating visual clutter during high-stress moments.",
      "where": "07:16 to 07:20, 10:35",
      "severity": "minor",
      "suggestion": "Move the wolf snatch telemetry and timer boxes to the edge of the HUD or integrate them as world-space audio/visual cues."
    },
    {
      "problem": "The trial trial course (Glenbrae Trial) feels overly rigid and punishing compared to the organic open-field herding of the rest of the campaign.",
      "where": "01:25 to 02:54",
      "severity": "minor",
      "suggestion": "Make the gate trigger zones slightly more forgiving and provide clearer ground-painted drift lines to guide turns."
    },
    {
      "problem": "The flat grass texture and repetitive ground details in standard daytime maps look a bit stark and mobile-game-ish before the fog or snow sets in.",
      "where": "00:10 to 00:24",
      "severity": "cosmetic",
      "suggestion": "Add more procedural foliage tufts, flowers, wind ripples, and soil variation across the meadow turf."
    }
  ],
  "boredom_points": [
    "Trudging at walking pace behind a slow-moving cluster on long straight dirt paths when no wolves are near (e.g. 08:18 - 08:30).",
    "Waiting out the last thirty seconds of the Night Watch level when all wolves have already backed off (16:00 - 16:23)."
  ],
  "confusions": [
    "At first glance, understanding whether 'creep' or 'bark' is better against stubborn sheep like Old Angus until the text tutorial explicitly clarifies it.",
    "How wolf aggro works across water - it isn't immediately obvious whether wolves can swim or ford the stream until they cross over."
  ],
  "wish_list": [
    "A free-roam endless practice paddock or custom weather sandbox mode.",
    "More shepherd whistled commands and customizable dog coats.",
    "A playable third-person camera mode behind Pip."
  ],
  "one_line_review": "Equal parts soothing pastoral simulator and nerve-shredding wolf thriller - an absolute gem of an indie herding game."
}
